chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

I asked Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) about a man who died and bequeathed the emancipation of a Muslim slave for thirty dinars, but the amount specified could not be found. He (peace be upon him) said: 'I see that they should increase upon that which has been named.' I said: 'And if they cannot find it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let them buy from the general wealth of the people, provided it is not from a Nasibi (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt).'

key_terms.عُرْضِ النَّاسِ: The general wealth/assets of the people (or the deceased's general assets)
key_terms.نَاصِباً: Nasibi (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically the Imams)
key_terms.نَسَمَةٍ: A single person/soul (referring to a slave)

ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a bequest for freeing a slave if the specified amount is insufficient?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'itq' (manumission) by establishing that if the designated funds are insufficient, the heirs must supplement the amount from the estate's general assets rather than reducing the slave's value. The specific condition that the source be 'not Nasibi' reflects the Shia emphasis on purifying wealth from those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring the spiritual merit of the bequest is preserved. This ruling underscores the priority of fulfilling charitable bequests even when resources are limited, provided the origin of the funds is religiously sound.
